How do coalition governments work in parliamentary systems?
In proportional systems, no single party often wins a majority. Parties negotiate to form a coalition, sharing cabinet posts and policy priorities to govern together.
Does that mean they always compromise?
Yes. Coalition partners typically sign an agreement outlining shared policies. But compromises can also create instability if disagreements emerge.
Very common. Countries like Germany, the Netherlands, and Italy almost always have coalition governments due to highly proportional electoral systems.
Some appreciate that coalitions reflect broader representation. Others see them as messy or slow, especially if governments collapse and trigger early elections.
